study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Martin et al., Drug and Alcohol Dependence Reports, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Sex differences in normative modeling of cortical thickness in cannabis use disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The CUD participant data (n=72) was collected at a single site (Medical University of South Carolina) using a Siemens 3T Prisma scanner. The normative model was pre-trained: the NOMIS (NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics) tool provides normative z-scores derived from a large sample of healthy adults (n=6909, ages 18-100) from Potvin et al. (2022, 2017, 2016). The authors did not train the normative model themselves but applied the pre-trained NOMIS software to their CUD sample.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The present study used pre-treatment baseline data from two clinical trials for CUD at the Medical University of South Carolina." ... "T1-weighted MRI was obtained from a single site using a Siemens 3 T Prisma (Siemens Healthineers)." ... "The aseg.stats file for each participant was then input into the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which computes normative z-scores of participant-level measurements relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18-100 (n = 6909), accounting for age, sex, intracranial volume, and image quality (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016)."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The single-site CUD sample (n=72, 50 males, 22 females) was the target clinical dataset. Participants' T1-weighted images were processed through FreeSurfer and then NOMIS to obtain normative z-scores. The pre-trained NOMIS normative model (based on n=6909 healthy adults) served as the reference population. The authors did not perform any normative model training, validation, or testing themselves.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The authors used the pre-trained NOMIS tool. The normative reference sample consists of n=6909 healthy adults. Because the model was pre-trained by Potvin et al. and applied as-is, the train/validation/test split details are not reported in this paper. The overall normative sample size of 6909 is stated directly.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "...the NOrmative Morphometry Image Statistics (NOMIS) software which computes normative z-scores of participant-level measurements relative to a large sample of healthy adults ages 18-100 (n = 6909), accounting for age, sex, intracranial volume, and image quality (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016). The normative values for 1344 FreeSurfer-segmented brain regions were derived from k-fold cross-validated regression models..."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The normative model (NOMIS) was built from healthy adults aged 18-100 (n=6909). Mean, SD, median, and IQR of the normative reference sample are not reported in this paper; only the age range is stated. The train-phase split details are not provided as the model was pre-trained externally (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016).

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex breakdown of the NOMIS normative reference sample (n=6909) is not reported in this paper. The NOMIS model accounts for sex as a covariate, but the sex composition of the normative sample is not described here. This information may be available in the original NOMIS publications (Potvin et al., 2022, 2017, 2016).
